To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermogenic response to CR is different between male and female rats.

the thermogenic capacity of BAT in female rats is more reduced during caloric restriction (CR), and that this reduction is associated with a decrease in mitochondrial differentiation and lipolytic capacity.

the thermogenic response to caloric restriction is gender-dependent and that female rats, which have higher BAT recruitment under ad libitum feeding, have lower thermogenic response during caloric restriction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the gender differences in the response to a caloric restriction in brown adipose tissues.
the study of sex differences in brown adipose thermogenesis during CR.
the mechanisms underlying the gender-dependent inactivation of BAT thermogenesis during CR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CR inactivates BAT thermogenesis in female rats more than in males, and this could be due to an impaired mitochondrial differentiation process and a less favourable balance of adrenergic receptors.
CR in female rats induces a greater inactivation of the BAT thermogenic activity than in males, probably due to a more pronounced reduction of BAT recruitment and mitochondrial differentiation.
the inactivation of BAT thermogenic activity during CR is a sex-dependent phenomenon.

the female rat is better prepared than the male rat to deal with energy restriction, at least in terms of thermogenesis.
females rats are more resistant to weight loss than males and this could be due to the higher BAT thermogenic capacity and the greater inactivation of this organ under CR conditions.
female rats have higher BAT thermogenic activity and higher energy conservation during CR.

the gender differences found in the thermogenic response of BAT to CR could be a mechanism for the greater resistance to weight loss observed in females.
